title: Mathematics Practice Test 1 - Mathematics - Function Transformations
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let the function $f$ be defined as $f(x) = -9x^2$. In the standard $(x,y)$ coordinate plane, the graph of $y = f(x)$ undergoes a transformation such that the result is the graph of $y = f(x) - 4$. Under this transformation the graph of $y = f(x)$ is:
options: stretched horizontally by a factor of 4.
stretched vertically by a factor of 4.
questions.explain: Subtracting a positive constant from a function $f(x)$ (e.g., $f(x) - 4$) causes a vertical shift of the graph downwards by that constant number of units. Thus, the graph is shifted downward 4 units.
